brief: Weekly retail-flows note. September closed as the weakest month for retail activity since December 2024, with flows this week at $4.1B versus a 12-month average of $6.8B, as retail favored ETFs over single stocks. ETF demand weakened toward 2025 Momentum Unwind levels on declines in International, Crypto and Commodity ETFs, partly offset by the largest-ever rotation into long-end Treasury ETFs (+5.4z), led by a record +6.1z inflow into TLT as yields kept rising. Mag7 names dominated single-stock buying (NVDA, TSLA, GOOG/L, AMZN bought; AAPL, MSFT, META sold) while every other sector outside Tech was net sold. Rising Treasury yields, now at 22-year highs, coincided with small caps underperforming large caps: retail stayed net sellers of Russell 2000 stocks, where short interest is now at the 99.8th percentile, and net buyers of Russell 1000. Energy flows flipped mildly negative even as Middle East oil exports recovered toward pre-war levels and crude held near $100. Retail positioned minimally ahead of Micron's earnings, which then beat with guidance above expectations.
